hook: What happens if the police **arrest** me?
hook_q: What are my rights if I am arrested?

slides.title: You must be **told why.**
slides.body: If you're arrested without a warrant, police must at once tell you the full details of the offence, or the other grounds, for your arrest.

slides.title: Bailable offence? You must be told **about bail.**
slides.body: If you're arrested without a warrant and not accused of a non-bailable offence, police must tell you that you are entitled to be released on bail and can arrange sureties.

slides.title: Someone you name **gets told.**
slides.body: Police must at once inform a relative, friend or person you name about the arrest and where you're held. They must tell you of this right once you reach the police station.

slides.title: You can **meet a lawyer.**
slides.body: If police arrest and question you, you can meet an advocate of your choice during the questioning, though not for all of it.

slides.title: A **medical check** soon after arrest.
slides.body: A government medical officer (or, if none is available, a registered medical practitioner) must examine you soon after the arrest. A copy of the report goes to you or your nominee.

timeline.text: Police must take or send you, **without unnecessary delay**, before a Magistrate or the officer in charge of a police station.
Without a Magistrate's special order, you can't be held longer than this. Travel time to the court is not counted.

slides.title: In custody? **Free legal aid.**
slides.body: A person in custody who has to defend a case is entitled to free legal services. NALSA's helpline is 15100.
slides.ref: Legal Services Authorities Act 1987 · Sec 12(g) · NALSA

sources: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 – Sections 38, 47, 48, 53, 57, 58 (indiacode.nic.in; NCRB, ncrb.mha.gov.in)
caption:
Arrested? These are the rights the law gives you. 👇

1️⃣ Arrested without a warrant? Police must tell you the full grounds of arrest at once
2️⃣ Not accused of a non-bailable offence? Police must also tell you you're entitled to bail
3️⃣ A relative, friend or person you name must be told about the arrest and where you're held
4️⃣ You can meet an advocate of your choice during questioning (not for all of it)
5️⃣ A medical check soon after arrest, with a copy of the report
6️⃣ You must be taken before a Magistrate. No more than 24 hours in police custody without a Magistrate's order (travel time excluded)

Source: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 – Sections 38, 47, 48, 53, 57, 58; Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 – Section 12; NALSA
